_note: Strange gear: the finds a shop turns up that are not in the printed catalog. Cyberpunk RED prints a gear list; it does not print a hush wrap or a sound puck, so everything here is ours. Each find is ONE base object with ONE capability and at most one limit, and a capability is a rule the engine enforces, not a description: `quiet` removes a `loud` observation the turn it is used, `remote` removes `seen`, `quick` halves the in-world time a Life turn's activity takes. Nothing here may grant a die, a DV, damage or an outcome. A find's identity is its item id (gadget.<base>.<capability>.<limit>.<variant>), so its name, price and contract are derived from that id every time and never stored, and an id this file cannot read is not a gadget at all.

quiet.label: Quiet
quiet.contract: Used on something, the act is not heard: the city does not record it as loud.

remote.label: Remote
remote.contract: It does its work where you left it, so you are not there to be seen doing it: the city does not record you as seen for that act.

quick.label: Quick
quick.contract: Whatever you use it for takes half the time it otherwise would.

unreliable.label: Temperamental
unreliable.contract: It does not always work: roll a d6 when you use it, and on a 1 or 2 it does nothing.

single_use.label: One use
single_use.contract: It works once and is spent.

conspicuous.label: Conspicuous
conspicuous.contract: Nobody forgets seeing it: using it means you are seen.

bases.what: A roll of dense acoustic foam tape you wind round a tool, a hinge or a latch before you go to work on it.
Bolt cutters with packed, rubber-sleeved jaws that bite through a chain or a padlock shackle with a soft crunch instead of a crack.
A tube of clear silicone gel that kills the squeak in a hinge, the rattle in a vent cover and the click in a lock.
A coin-sized speaker that sticks to anything and plays one stored sound — a knock, a voice, a phone ringing — when you press the paired fob.
A spring clip that clamps onto a switch, a latch or a lever and throws it when you send the signal from your Agent.
A wind-up mechanical timer you wire to whatever you want tripped, so it happens while you are somewhere else entirely.
A palm-sized tracked toy drone with a little grabber arm, steered from your Agent, that goes where you would rather not.
A compressed-air multi-driver that runs panel screws, cover plates and bolts out in seconds.
A fold-out canvas roll that puts every tool exactly where the hand reaches for it.
A pick gun that snaps a cheap pin tumbler lock's pins in one go: the same lock, just faster.

quirks: A logo has been taped over, badly.
Somebody's initials are scratched into it.
It still has a corporate inventory tag on it.
It has been repainted matte black by hand.
The instructions are printed in Korean.
There is a sticker of a cartoon cat on it.
It is newer than anything else on the shelf.

finds._note: How many finds a shop turns up in a stock week: one d6, read on this table, shifted by the shop's own `finds` in place-shops.json (salvage and pawn shops lean in). Most weeks most shops have nothing strange. Finds are sold one at a time.
